newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RALLYING-ERIKSSON STUNS SAINZ IN NEW ZEALAND.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-ERIKSSON STUNS SAINZ IN NEW ZEALAND.

text.p: Kenneth Eriksson put the Subaru team back in command of the New Zealand Rally on Monday when his early charge in the opening stage of the second leg left overnight leader Carlos Sainz labouring in pursuit throughout a demanding day.
The Swede eclipsed his Spanish rival by 39 seconds on the first section, the longest and toughest, to open up a clear advantage.

Double world champion Sainz had held a 12 seconds advantage overnight in his Ford Escort but was left to struggle after Eriksson's blistering performance at Te Koraha. Despite steady progress, Sainz was still eight seconds adrift at the end of the day.

"Everything felt really good this morning," said Eriksson. "I had a good feeling and I was totally focused on taking Carlos. The stage was quite narrow in places, but our Subaru Impreza car felt really well-suited to the conditions. It all just came together as we hoped it would."
Eriksson is now on course for his first victory in New Zealand, a triumph which could also extend Subaru's dominance of the event, at world championship level, to three successive victories.

Eriksson's team mate Colin McRae of Britain has won the event three times in the last four years, but retired on Sunday after a camshaft belt failure while leading. His bid for a second world title had been boosted earlier by the retirement of current leader and defending champion Tommi Makinen of Finland, who rolled his Mitsubishi early in the first leg.
Sainz pressed hard in the closing stages and succeeded in reducing his disadvantage. Eriksson blamed the reduction in his lead on misjudged tyre choices on stages 14 and 15.

"We have done a lot of development work with Pirelli," he said. "The tyres we brought with us to New Zealand have definitely given us an edge. But we slipped up on two of the stages and took a hard compound when we really should have taken a softer one."
